handoff: Review #1: 3 blocking — F1 CI missing from non-holder view (B18/AC3; add RemotePort CI read + gh/glab/FakeRemote/contract), F9 lastBoundary treats mirror/waits-for-input/started commits as boundaries (B18/B19), F13 store record-ref F1 property test times out (real failure; bound it, 10 isolated + 3 full-tier runs). Minor: cache written by view and never tidied, swallowed fetch errors, prose in --json where[], heldElsewhereKeys scope, weak AC5/AC3 tests, two record caches vs slice 16.

findings.title: Non-holder view shows the PR but not its CI (B18, AC3)
findings.detail:
AC3: 'then it shows ... the PR and CI'. B18: 'show the claim, the branch, the PR with its CI'. formatElsewhere prints only '- PR: #N draft, open — url (seen …)'; ElsewhereView.pr (PrView) carries no CI; RemotePort (packages/core/src/ports.ts:323) has no method reporting CI and RemotePullRequest has no CI field. The AC3 test (non-holder-views.test.ts:365) asserts no CI either. handoff records this as a deliberate omission ('no port reports CI'); it is not an ambiguity.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Add a RemotePort method (or a field on findPullRequest) reporting the PR head's CI state (e.g. pending|success|failure|none): gh (`gh pr checks`/statusCheckRollup) and glab (pipeline status) adapters with recorded fixtures, FakeRemote, a case in packages/adapters/test/contract/remoteContract; observe stores it with the PR seen for stories held elsewhere; ElsewhereView/formatElsewhere print it; the AC3 test sets CI on the FakeRemote PR and asserts it in markdown and --json.

findings.title: lastBoundary reports a step that has not ended (B18, B19)
findings.detail:
lastBoundary takes the newest commit with Norn-Story=<key> and a Norn-Step trailer, and treats the oldest such commit as the start (`steps.length > 1`). But non-boundary commits also carry Norn-Step = the step still running: the mirror commit (packages/core/src/decide/story.ts:299, `commitFor(..., su?.state?.step)`), 'waits for input' (packages/core/src/decide/agent.ts:409), 'started' / 'prompt re-sent' (agent.ts:138, :471), round starts (story.ts:504). So a story in implement whose issue is edited, or whose agent asks, shows 'last boundary: implement' before implement ended. Conversely, when the start commit is not made (nothing to commit), the first real boundary is taken for the start and B shows 'no boundary pushed yet'. B19: 'I want the view to say so instead of a step, so that I am not shown a guess'; B18: 'the last step from the last boundary commit'. Tests cover only the clean shape (AC3 after one done, AC4 with only the start commit).
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Identify boundary commits by what they are (an outcome/transition trailer, or the `<step>.<outcome> →` subject the boundary commit carries), not by position; add AC4/AC3 cases with a 'waits for input' or mirror commit during implement and with no start commit.

findings.title: The record cache is written and pruned by the view, and never cleaned by tidy
findings.detail:
readRecord unpacks into <machine dir>/record-cache/<story>/<sha>/ and rmSyncs sibling shas, reached from loadProjectView (load.ts:~555) on every `status`/`story view`. D6 sanctions a cache 'the way the base branch's specs are cached', but that cache (baseFactsPath) is written by observe, not by the view. Nothing in cli/src/commands/tidy.ts or store/src/trace.ts removes record-cache/<story>/ for stories no longer held elsewhere or finished, so folders accumulate per story forever (bounded to one sha per story only).
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Unpack in the tick right after fetchElsewhere (views only read; a miss shows 'not unpacked yet'), and have tidy remove record-cache/<story>/ folders whose story is no longer held elsewhere.

findings.title: Concurrent views: pruning sibling shas can make another view show zero units with no error
findings.detail:
View A unpacks a new sha and deletes sibling sha folders while view B reads the old one; B's readdirSync/readState fail into `continue`/[] and it renders no units and no error. Unreadable state files are also dropped silently (`if (!st.ok) continue`) instead of landing in RecordRead.error (S2: a failing file is reported, not skipped).
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Prune only from the tick or tidy; record a unit whose state.json fails validation in `error`.

findings.title: Targeted fetch failures are swallowed
findings.detail:
observe: `fetchElsewhere(...).catch(() => undefined)` hides an ls-remote/fetch failure from cache.last_error, so a non-holder silently shows stale records as current. human.ts:108 (remoteTarget) does the same, so a mailbox verb acts on a stale local record without saying so. load.ts `heldElsewhereKeys(...).catch(() => [])` leaves nothing in view.errors. The human.ts fetch itself is bounded (one ls-remote of record names + one fetch of the story's branches and its one record ref) and narrower than the full fetch it replaces, which is acceptable under D6 ('story answer|approve fetch the one story they need'). (The same catch-all already wraps fetchNornRefs at observe/index.ts:197, so this follows precedent.)
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Let the sync catch record the error (drop the inner catch in observe); in human.ts surface a warning when the fetch fails.

findings.title: Person-facing sentences built into the view data (ElsewhereView.where), emitted by --json
findings.detail:
elsewhereView pushes 'record as of … — gh-9 now keeps its record on …' and 'run state is on …'s machine — ask them to run …' into `where`, which `norn story view --json` prints (story-view.ts:35; view data already carries free text such as reason/summary, hence minor). P8: the machine contract is JSON, never prose; the data (policy, current, expires_at, holder) is already in the view, so the sentences belong in formatElsewhere/formatInbox.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Replace `where: string[]` with data (e.g. record_kept_current, run_state_on) and build the sentences in format.ts.

findings.title: lastBoundary walks the whole history on every view
findings.detail:
`git log --format=… <ref>` with no range runs over all of main's history for every story held elsewhere on every status/story view; cost grows with the repo. Object.fromEntries keeps only the last of repeated trailer keys.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Limit to `<base>..<ref>` or --grep on the story trailer.

findings.title: fetchElsewhere doc says it fetches slice branches; `<story>-*` does not match `<story>/<nn>-…`
findings.detail:
Slice branches are `<story>/<nn>-<slug>` (the removed human.ts code looked them up as `${story}/${nn}-`); the refspec `+refs/heads/<story>-*` fetches only the story branch.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Fix the comment (slice branches are not needed by the ACs).

findings.title: Duplicated helpers
findings.detail:
`const minute = (iso) => iso.slice(0, 16).replace("T", " ")` in format.ts and load.ts; the counter string `${c.name} ${c.value}${c.max !== null ? `/${c.max}` : ""}` built twice in format.ts; `"local" | "remote"` retyped instead of taken from the config schema type. observe/index.ts:202 also spawns one readLocalClaim per prSeenIn key outside the snapshot on every tick.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: One helper each; reuse the heldElsewhereKeys pass in observe.

findings.title: heldElsewhereKeys does not restrict to open stories and drops same-holder clones
findings.detail:
D6: 'A tick fetches refs/norn/runs/<story> only for open stories this checkout shows and another heartbeat holds.' Every local claim ref counts (no open-issue check; expired claims count). The `holder !== me.holder && heartbeat_id !== me.heartbeat_id` test excludes a second clone on the same user@host (different heartbeat, same holder), whose stories are then neither fetched nor shown.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Filter by the open issues observe lists; decide whether same-holder other-heartbeat should count (probably yes: `||` or heartbeat only) and test it.

findings.title: AC5/AC2/AC3 tests weaker than their claims
findings.detail:
AC5: gh-10 (held by B) never has a record ref on the remote (B's config was switched to local in AC2), so 'B's refs hold gh-9 only' would pass even if B fetched its own story's ref; gh-4 is excluded only because it has no claim; 'unpacked once per record commit' is a directory listing, not a second view that does no unpack. AC3: heartbeat/expiry are expected from the command's own --json (v.renewed_at), circular; B18's `status` side is not asserted for a local story with a boundary. AC2: the switch is made in B's working tree only, not by the team (pushed config).
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Push a record ref for gh-10 before B's tick; read the claim blob from the bare remote for expected times; assert status for AC3; assert a second view leaves the cache folder's mtime unchanged.

findings.title: remoteTarget rewrite touches the mailbox path (slice 13) without a test here
findings.detail:
D6 lists `story answer|approve` fetching the one story they need, so the change is defensible, but it is untested in this slice and under `local` with no ref it now returns null (falls back to the stale local copy).
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Leave a note for gh-195/13 to cover it.

findings.title: record-ref F1 property test is not deterministic in time (real failure, not a flake)
findings.detail:
'F1: packed tree … under autocrlf and a clean filter' (from slice 08, on the story branch) timed out at the 20 s per-test limit in this slice's parallel integration run and failed 1 of 3 isolated runs in slice 16. By the flake protocol (flake only if it passes every isolated run) it is a real failure. It builds ~25 git repos inside one 20 s test. Supervisor assigns the fix to this slice's rework.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Keep the property's strength but make it bounded in time: fewer seeded trees with the same coverage of CRLF / clean filter / exec bit / nested / non-ASCII cases, one shared repo, or an explicit per-test timeout justified by measurement. Prove it with 10 isolated runs and 3 full integration-tier runs, recorded in handoff.md.

findings.title: Second cache for unpacked records diverges from slice 16's archive cache
findings.detail:
This slice adds `<machine dir>/record-cache/<story>/<sha>/` (recordCacheDir, readRecord). Sibling slice gh-195/16 (not yet integrated) adds `archivedRecordDir` in packages/store/src/record-ref.ts, unpacking a ref once per record commit into `<machine dir>/archive/<story>/<sha>/`, plus unpackRecordSync, localRecordRefs and fetchRecords. Two caches for the same thing (record commit → unpacked tree). Not blocking for this slice alone.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: When the slices meet, converge on one cache keyed by record sha with one fetch helper, and have tidy bound it (see F2).
